subject: Failure to run a multivariate count model

messages.author: 72d5cfa8c4ed99f4
messages.subject: Failure to run a multivariate count model
parts:
Dear Stan-users
I want to update a model with multivariate count data (common in biodiversity modelling). I use a scaled inverse Wishart to express the covariance for the multivariate normal distribution of logged intensities. Since my data is counts, I would like to use a Poisson process at the last step to derive the likelihood.
My problem is that adding this last step does not work. I can run the model using logged counts as data on the multivariate normal directly, but as soon as I add the observation process (the Poisson distribution on data) the sampler get NaN values on the multivariate normal and a lot of other errors. This is frustrating since the model without the Poisson step works. 

I have tried adding initials with no success. 

I attach an artificial generated data and code with the two alternative models. 

It would be much appreciated if anyone could hint what is wrong : )
. 
~Ullrika

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Failure to run a multivariate count model
parts:
We recommend using a scaled LKJ prior for covariance, because
it's easier to reason about as a prior (unless you have prior
data, in which case inverse Wishart is conjugate). We also
recommend using the much more efficient and stable
Cholesky-factor parameterization, which LKJ supports. That may
solve the problem if the NaN are coming from numerical instability.
Otherwise, you'll need to track down what the parameters are that
are getting generated for the Poisson (or poisson_log, which takes
the log mean/variance as a parameter rather than the mean/variance).

Also, the data may not be consistent with a Poisson process. We
tend to use overdispersed models, but those are even trickier to fit.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Failure to run a multivariate count model
parts: This model is an over-dispersed construction via the Gaussian prior on the lambda with covariance, A.  I have found some difficulty to fit such models for multivariate lambda where the covariance matrix, A, is *not* diagonal (even under a more flexible prior than IW for A).

messages.author: 71c315ee557ff234
messages.subject: Re: Failure to run a multivariate count model
parts:
Dear Ullrika,

due to sd 10 in normal and poisson values > 30 you in into (over/under) flows in poisson, eg. exp(20)^-40 -> 0 -> log(0) -> NaN

Andre

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Failure to run a multivariate count model
parts:
log(0) is -infinity, not NaN. It might raise a pole error in
some implementations, but won't raise a domain error.
See:

http://www.cplusplus.com/reference/cmath/log/

Stan follows the standard's behavior for built-in functions.

But what can happen is that downstream, you might try to
add positive infinity to negative infinity, which gives you NaN.
Or divide.

- Bob

messages.author: d0d4a852dcbd9f5b
messages.subject: Re: Failure to run a multivariate count model
parts:
Hi Ulrika,

I think the problems stems from the fact that you declare lambda in your model block. If you move the declaration to the parameter block, I think your model with poisson will work. I never grok why exactly but parameters with a distribution need to go into the parameters block. In the model block, you can declare parameters that are deterministically related to other parameters. 

For what it's worth. The results as is look fine with chains = 4, iter = 200 and you can also use cores = 4 (or whatever is applicable) to run the chains in parallel. I still encountered quite some numerical issues with the positive definiteness of LDLT_factor. You might want to look into the LKJ prior and the Cholesky decomposition which are much more stan and numerical friendly. Section 6.14 in the 2.12 Stan User's guide might be helpful for that.

Stijn

Thank you for the suggestions. Moving the declaration of lambda from the model to the parameter block solved the sampling problem. We can now run the model. 

Yes, we are actually testing different priors for the covariance matrix and now, when we are able to run the model in stan, we can do all the wonderful decompositions that we planned for.

~Ullrika
